title: How Trump’s FBI Purge Saved Graham And Clyburn From Bribery Investigation

 Marita Vlachou Tue, 20 October 2026 at 2:06 pm UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. On March 3, 2020, Sen. Lindsey Graham walked into a private dining room at Charlie Palmer Steak in Washington, D.C. Graham's time was expensive. He was meeting with two executives and a lobbyist from a Hawaiian naval defense contractor called Navatek. And he had required them to commit to $40,000 in campaign contributions for a 45-minute meeting.
 Navatek's CEO, Martin Kao, was confident that was all the time he needed.
 "Shoot all he has to really do is stop by and say 'yes,'" Kao wrote to a Navatek lobbyist and a fellow executive the day before, in an email seen by ProPublica. "That should only take a minute and he's on his way. We don't need to pretend we give a **** about each other."
 Also in the news: Hegseth Meets Netanyahu In Unannounced Visit To Israel, Axios Reports 
 At the dinner, Graham ate little and talked a lot. But Kao got the "yes" he was hoping for: Graham agreed to steer a $10 million government contract Navatek's way in his native South Carolina, Kao later recounted to the FBI. In exchange, he said, Graham asked Kao to pledge a total of $100,000 to his reelection campaign.
